sentences.en: It's all true, or it ought to be.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是真的，或者至少应该是真的。

sentences.en: So said Winston Churchill of the legend of King Arthur.
sentences.zh: 温斯顿·丘吉尔在谈到亚瑟王传说时曾这样说。

sentences.en: Romantic historical story or just an invented myth?
sentences.zh: 这是浪漫的历史故事，还是纯粹虚构的神话？

sentences.en: Well, welcome to The Rest is History with me, Dominic Samarov, and my very own Mordred, Tom Holland.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《历史的余韵》，我是多米尼克·萨马罗夫，还有我的专属莫德雷德——汤姆·霍兰德。

sentences.en: Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆。

sentences.en: I should say that in the script, in the script, Dominic, it says my very own Galahad.
sentences.zh: 我得说，多米尼克，剧本里写的是我的专属加拉哈德。

sentences.en: I know, but I was never going to read that out.
sentences.zh: 我知道，但我从没打算把它读出来。

sentences.en: I was never going to read that out.

sentences.en: Very subtly done.
sentences.zh: 做得真隐晦。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I was hoping you wouldn't know this.
sentences.zh: 我本来希望你不知道这个。

sentences.en: So let's kick off.
sentences.zh: 那我们开始吧。

sentences.en: This is a great subject.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很棒的主题。

sentences.en: King Arthur was my very first historical enthusiasm.
sentences.zh: 亚瑟王是我最早的历史兴趣所在。

sentences.en: So I read the Lady Bird King Arthur books.
sentences.zh: 我读过《瓢虫》版的亚瑟王丛书。

sentences.en: I read Antonia Fraser's book about the Knights of the Round Table.
sentences.zh: 我读过安东尼娅·弗雷泽写的关于圆桌骑士的书。

sentences.en: And I think I read those before I read anything about real kings.
sentences.zh: 我想我在读任何关于真实国王的历史之前，就先读了这些。

sentences.zh: 很多对历史感兴趣的人大概都是这样，对吧？

sentences.en: You start with King Arthur and Robin Hood, and then you get into the enclosures and dissolution of the monasteries and all the really exciting, glamorous subjects.
sentences.zh: 你从亚瑟王和罗宾汉开始，然后深入研究圈地运动、修道院解散，以及所有那些真正令人兴奋、充满魅力的课题。

sentences.en: Yes.

sentences.zh: 读到圈地运动时，总会有一种模糊的感觉。

sentences.en: But nights with penance are just a lot more fun.
sentences.zh: 但苦修之夜显然要有趣得多。

sentences.en: And I suppose hanging over this entire theme is the obvious one, which is summed up very effectively by Tom McTague, the UK correspondent for The Atlantic, who asks,
sentences.zh: 我想，笼罩在这个主题之上的，是一个显而易见的问题，正如《大西洋月刊》英国通讯员汤姆·麦克泰格所总结的那样，他问道：

sentences.en: Arthur, who, what, why, how?
sentences.zh: 亚瑟是谁，什么，为什么，怎么回事？

sentences.en: I guess you could express that as basically, did he exist?
sentences.zh: 我想你可以把它简化为：他到底存不存在？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So, Dominic, are you a sceptic or a believer?
sentences.zh: 那么，多米尼克，你是怀疑论者还是相信者？

sentences.en: Well, that's it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，就是这样。

sentences.en: To my mind, I guess, if I like to believe that Arthur existed, of course, because I'm a romantic.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，我当然愿意相信亚瑟存在，因为我是一个浪漫主义者。

sentences.en: But ultimately, I suppose my instinct is that there were multiple Arthurs, right?
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，我的直觉是历史上存在多个亚瑟，对吧？

sentences.en: That probably there were multiple warlords and generals, some of them Roman leftovers, some of them Celtic, some of them maybe even Germanic,
sentences.zh: 可能存在多位军阀和将军，有些是罗马遗留的，有些是凯尔特人的，甚至有些可能是日耳曼人的，

sentences.en: who sort of fed into the Arthur legend at the end of Roman Britain in that sort of period that we think of as the Dark Ages.
sentences.zh: 他们在罗马不列颠末期，也就是我们所说的黑暗时代，共同构成了亚瑟传说的原型。

sentences.en: And that, you know, it wasn't completely invented that there must have been grains of truth, as there always are in historical myths.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这并非完全虚构，历史神话中总会有真实的成分。

sentences.en: But anyway, Tom, this is your field.
sentences.zh: 但不管怎样，汤姆，这是你的领域。

sentences.en: You're on home turf.
sentences.zh: 这是你的主场。

sentences.en: You should be answering this question.
sentences.zh: 你应该来回答这个问题。

sentences.en: I don't think he existed.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他存在。

sentences.en: You know this word euhemerism, the idea that in the distant past, you have mortals, kings, powerful figures who go on over the course of time, become elevated and end up as gods.
sentences.zh: 你知道“欧赫迈罗斯主义”这个词吗？就是说在遥远的过去，凡人、国王、权贵随着时间的推移，被神化并最终成为了神。

sentences.en: But I think that Arthur is a kind of interesting example of something going the opposite way, that I think he's essentially a kind of mythical figure, a figure of folklore,
sentences.zh: 但我认为亚瑟是一个有趣的例子，情况恰恰相反。我认为他本质上是一个神话人物，一个民间传说中的人物，

sentences.en: who gets attached to a specific historical narrative.
sentences.zh: 被附加到了一个特定的历史叙事中。

sentences.en: And the reason that that can work is that, as you said, the setting for Arthur are the century, maybe two centuries after the collapse of Roman Britain,
sentences.zh: 之所以能行得通，是因为正如你所说，亚瑟的背景设定在罗马不列颠崩溃后的一个世纪，甚至两个世纪，

sentences.en: which is the two century period that really we struggle to fit a narrative onto it.
sentences.zh: 那两个世纪是我们极难构建叙事的时期。

sentences.en: We have so few written sources and the evidence from archaeology, from genetics and everything is so contradictory and so complex.
sentences.zh: 我们拥有的书面资料太少，而考古学、遗传学等方面的证据又如此矛盾且复杂。

sentences.en: But in a sense, if you wanted to slot a mythical figure and pretend, imagine, cast him, construct him as someone who had actually existed, that's the period that you would do it.
sentences.zh: 但从某种意义上说，如果你想安插一个神话人物，假装、想象、塑造他为一个真实存在过的人，那确实是最好的时期。

sentences.en: But I think that,
sentences.zh: 但我认为，

sentences.en: I guess there are two problems really.
sentences.zh: 我想这确实有两个问题。

sentences.en: One is that the sources that mention Arthur are incredibly late.
sentences.zh: 一是提到亚瑟的资料来源非常晚。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So they're well after the event.
sentences.zh: 所以它们离事件发生的时间已经很久了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there's a description of a raid that was launched by some Welsh-speaking Britons from the region of Edinburgh against what's thought to be the Roman fort of Cattaric.
sentences.zh: 有一段关于突袭的描述，是由爱丁堡地区讲威尔士语的布立吞人发起的，目标被认为是罗马的卡塔里克要塞。

sentences.en: And this is set about, well, that's 600.
sentences.zh: 这大约发生在600年左右。

sentences.en: And the guy who is describing it claims, at the beginning of the poem, a guy called Anerin says, I am narrating it.
sentences.zh: 描述它的那个人，一个叫阿内林的诗人在诗的开头声称，我正在叙述它。

sentences.en: And he's supposed to have lived around 600.
sentences.zh: 他应该生活在600年左右。

sentences.en: And in that poem, there is a phrase that this warlord pulls off great feats, but he was not Arthur, is the phrase.
sentences.zh: 在那首诗中，有一句话说这位军阀立下了丰功伟绩，但“他不是亚瑟”，就是这句话。

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 噢，是的。

sentences.en: So if we can identify that at 600, then that is evidence for it being very early.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们能确定那是600年的话，那就是它非常早期的证据。

sentences.en: And Arthur being somebody that people will know and that people will say, is he an Arthur, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 而且亚瑟是一个人们会知道，并且会说“他是亚瑟吗，他不是吗”的人。

sentences.en: So that's pretty big, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以这很重要，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, doesn't that suggeSt...
sentences.zh: 我是说，这难道不暗示……

sentences.en: Except that.
sentences.zh: 除非……

sentences.en: Except that.
sentences.zh: 除非……

sentences.en: This is a poem that was first written down in the 9th century and the earliest manuscript we have of it is the 13th century.
sentences.zh: 这首诗最早是在9世纪写下的，我们现存最早的手稿是13世纪的。

sentences.en: So there's a lot of potential for Chinese whispers there.
sentences.zh: 所以这里面有很大的传讹空间。

sentences.en: And even if it was, you know, written in 600,
sentences.zh: 而且即使它真的是在600年写的，

sentences.en: he was no Arthur.
sentences.zh: “他不是亚瑟”。

sentences.en: I mean, Arthur could still be a mythical figure.
sentences.zh: 我是说，亚瑟仍然可能是一个神话人物。

sentences.en: Yes, like you'd say he was no Heracles or...
sentences.zh: 是的，就像你会说他不是赫拉克勒斯或者……

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: And then what about these people like Gildas?
sentences.zh: 那么像吉尔达斯这样的人呢？

sentences.en: So Gildas is somebody who writes about Arthur, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 吉尔达斯写过亚瑟，对吧？

sentences.en: Tell me about Gildas.
sentences.zh: 跟我说说吉尔达斯。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: So Gildas is probably...
sentences.zh: 吉尔达斯大概是……

sentences.en: Again, difficult to pin him down exactly, but he's probably writing about 500.
sentences.zh: 同样，很难确切地定位他，但他大概是在500年左右写作的。

sentences.en: And he does give a kind of garbled narrative of what's going on, even though it's completely shot through with all kinds of Old Testament imagery.
sentences.zh: 他确实提供了一种混乱的叙事，尽管其中充满了各种旧约意象。

sentences.en: So he's not writing a kind of straight history.
sentences.zh: 所以他写的不是那种直白的历史。

sentences.en: And he does give us...
sentences.zh: 他确实给了我们……

sentences.en: He gives us a portrait of a haughty tyrant who subsequently gets identified with a guy called Vortigern,
sentences.zh: 他描绘了一个傲慢的暴君，后来被认定为伏提庚，

sentences.en: inviting Saxon mercenaries in.
sentences.zh: 他邀请了撒克逊雇佣兵进入。

sentences.en: Then you have Britain imploding.
sentences.zh: 然后不列颠陷入了崩溃。

sentences.en: You have a state of warfare.
sentences.zh: 你处于战争状态。

sentences.en: And this conventionally is the period that you associate with Arthur, but it's not Arthur who is mentioned.
sentences.zh: 这通常是你与亚瑟联系在一起的时期，但提到的并不是亚瑟。

sentences.en: It's a guy called Ambrosius Aurelianus who is described as the last of the Romans.
sentences.zh: 是一个叫安布罗修斯·奥里利亚努斯的人，他被描述为最后的罗马人。

sentences.en: And Arthur isn't there.
sentences.zh: 亚瑟并不在那里。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's a yawning gap.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的空白。

sentences.en: So why does Gildas not mention Arthur?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么吉尔达斯没有提到亚瑟？

sentences.en: I guess there are various...
sentences.zh: 我想有各种……

sentences.en: But hold on.
sentences.zh: 等等。

sentences.en: Don't people think that Ambrosius Aurelianus is Arthur?
sentences.zh: 难道人们不认为安布罗修斯·奥里利亚努斯就是亚瑟吗？

sentences.en: That's a lot of the stuff that I've read.
sentences.zh: 我读过很多这样的东西。

sentences.en: People say, well, this is obviously Arthur.
sentences.zh: 人们说，这显然就是亚瑟。

sentences.en: That was his real name.
sentences.zh: 那是他的真名。

sentences.en: Is that just Balterdash?
sentences.zh: 那纯粹是胡说八道吗？

sentences.en: It's kind of quite desperate because he's not called Arthur.
sentences.zh: 这有点绝望，因为他并不叫亚瑟。

sentences.en: I mean, he's called Arthur.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他叫亚瑟。

sentences.en: He's just really honeSt.
sentences.zh: 他只是真的很诚实。

sentences.en: So why is Gildas not mentioning Arthur?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么吉尔达斯没有提到亚瑟？

sentences.en: It could be because he hasn't heard of him.
sentences.zh: 可能是因为他没听说过他。

sentences.en: So Arthur is operating in some other area of the country that Gildas hasn't heard.
sentences.zh: 所以亚瑟是在吉尔达斯没听说过的其他地区活动。

sentences.en: Or it could be that Gildas has a problem with Arthur.
sentences.zh: 或者可能是吉尔达斯对亚瑟有意见。

sentences.en: So in a lot of the early saints' lives that you get in Wales and other Celtic areas,
sentences.zh: 在威尔士和其他凯尔特地区流传的许多早期圣徒传记中，

sentences.en: Arthur is often cast as a kind of problematic figure who preys on the church.
sentences.zh: 亚瑟常被塑造成一个掠夺教会的问题人物。

sentences.en: So perhaps that's the reason.
sentences.zh: 所以也许这就是原因。

sentences.en: So he's been cancelled.
sentences.zh: 所以他被“取消”了。

sentences.en: Gildas has cancelled him.
sentences.zh: 吉尔达斯取消了他。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Or perhaps he just doesn't exiSt.
sentences.zh: 或者也许他根本不存在。

sentences.en: You know, he's an imaginary figure.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他是一个虚构的人物。

sentences.en: And I think that that's the likeliest explanation.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是最可能的解释。

sentences.en: Where Arthur does appear in what seems to be a historical record is in a Welsh series of texts, of chronicles and so on, that is attached to the name of a Welsh writer
sentences.zh: 亚瑟出现在历史记录中的地方，是在一系列威尔士文本、编年史等中，这些文本归于一位威尔士作家名下，

sentences.en: called Nennius.
sentences.zh: 叫内尼厄斯。

sentences.en: But again, it's all very confusing.
sentences.zh: 但同样，这一切都非常令人困惑。

sentences.en: And this is the one that gives a famous list of 12 battles that Arthur is supposed to have won, culminating in the Battle of Baden,
sentences.zh: 这就是那个著名的亚瑟赢得的12场战役列表，最终是巴登山战役，

sentences.en: which we can be fairly confident is a battle that was fought because Gildas mentions it.
sentences.zh: 我们可以相当肯定这是一场确实发生过的战役，因为吉尔达斯提到了它。

sentences.en: But he doesn't associate it with Arthur.
sentences.zh: 但他并没有把它与亚瑟联系起来。

sentences.en: He doesn't even specifically say that it's Ambrosius or Relianus who won the Battle of Baden.
sentences.zh: 他甚至没有明确说是安布罗修斯·奥里利亚努斯赢得了巴登山战役。
zh_words: 安布罗修斯·奥里利亚努斯

sentences.en: He doesn't say who the Battle of Baden was againSt.
sentences.zh: 他没有说巴登山战役是针对谁的。

sentences.en: He doesn't really provide a solid date for it.
sentences.zh: 他也没有提供确切的日期。

sentences.en: So the whole thing is a kind of, it's a mess.
sentences.zh: 所以整件事就是一团糟。

sentences.en: And I think that that being so, you've got to ask, well, why and how would the legend of Arthur emerge?
sentences.zh: 既然如此，你必须问，亚瑟的传说为什么以及如何出现？

sentences.en: And I think that it's pretty clear that what's going on is that you have a Welsh-speaking tradition that is very hostile to what it sees as a takeover of its lands by Saxons.
sentences.zh: 我认为很明显，发生的事情是，有一个讲威尔士语的传统，对它所认为的撒克逊人夺取其土地的行为非常敌视。

sentences.en: And likewise, in the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, you have a very similar account of Saxons and Angles sweeping westwards, conquering the homelands of the Britons,
sentences.zh: 同样，在《盎格鲁-撒克逊编年史》中，也有关于撒克逊人和盎格鲁人向西横扫，征服布立吞人家园的非常相似的记载，

sentences.en: pushing them into Wales, seen from the other side.
sentences.zh: 从另一面看，他们把他们赶进了威尔士。

sentences.en: And traditionally, this has been understood to be a historical narrative that the Romans withdraw, that the Britons invite in the Saxons.
sentences.zh: 传统上，这被理解为一种历史叙事：罗马人撤退，布立吞人邀请撒克逊人进入。

sentences.en: The Saxons then conquer what becomes England.
sentences.zh: 撒克逊人随后征服了后来成为英格兰的地区。

sentences.en: Arthur supposedly wins the Battle of Baden, keeps the Saxons at bay for a few decades.
sentences.zh: 亚瑟据称赢得了巴登山战役，将撒克逊人阻挡了几十年。

sentences.en: The Saxons then come back in.
sentences.zh: 撒克逊人随后又卷土重来。

sentences.en: And that's a kind of narrative that has been repeated and repeated and is still kind of widely held to.
sentences.zh: 这是一种被反复重复的叙事，至今仍被广泛接受。

sentences.en: But I think it's a fantastical one.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这是一个幻想。

sentences.en: That's not what actually the archaeological evidence shows and it's not what the genetic evidence shows.
sentences.zh: 考古证据和遗传证据显示的并不是这样。

sentences.en: Let me interrupt you.
sentences.zh: 让我打断你一下。

sentences.en: So modern sort of academic historians, very recently, especially if they're sort of quite woke, shall we say, they think that this is the wrong narrative
sentences.zh: 所以现代的一些学术历史学家，最近，特别是如果他们比较“觉醒”的话，他们认为这是错误的叙事，

sentences.en: because it presents immigration as kind of contested and it's all done with fire and sword.
sentences.zh: 因为它把移民描绘成一种对抗，一切都是通过火与剑完成的。

sentences.en: And they sort of argue, oh no, it was much more gradual and there was an assimilation.
sentences.zh: 他们争辩说，哦不，这是一个更渐进的过程，存在一种同化。

sentences.en: That the idea that the Saxons came in and they drove Arthur and the Britons all into Wales is all balderdash and it was this sort of multicultural process and all the rest of it.
sentences.zh: 那种认为撒克逊人进来并把亚瑟和布立吞人都赶到威尔士的想法全是胡说八道，这是一种多元文化的过程，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Do you buy all that?
sentences.zh: 你相信这一切吗？

sentences.en: Is that your take on it all?
sentences.zh: 这就是你对这一切的看法吗？

sentences.en: I don't think it's about woke anxieties about immigration.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这与对移民的“觉醒”焦虑有关。

sentences.en: I think it's about the fact that all the evidence on the ground, the archaeological evidence, shows very little sign and the genetic evidence
sentences.zh: 我认为这是因为实地所有的证据，考古证据，几乎没有显示出大规模入侵的迹象，而遗传证据

sentences.en: shows very little sign of a kind of mass invasion.
sentences.zh: 也几乎没有显示出大规模入侵的迹象。

sentences.en: Basically, the Angles and the Saxons, like the Welsh, they're all descended from the people who lived in Roman Britain.
sentences.zh: 基本上，盎格鲁人和撒克逊人，就像威尔士人一样，都是生活在罗马不列颠的人的后裔。

sentences.en: What seems to have happened is that, for reasons that we can't be absolutely certain about, that the eastern half of the former province of Britannia starts to identify culturally
sentences.zh: 似乎发生的事情是，出于我们无法完全确定的原因，不列颠前行省的东半部开始在文化上认同

sentences.en: with the kind of the Germanic reaches of the North Sea and it's a conscious reaction against Romanitas, against the ideals of Rome.
sentences.zh: 北海的日耳曼地区，这是对罗马性、对罗马理想的一种自觉反抗。

sentences.en: And almost as if in reaction to that, the western half of Britain, which had always been less Romanised, very, very radically starts to identify
sentences.zh: 几乎就像是对这种反抗的回应，一直以来受罗马化程度较低的英国西部，非常激进地开始认同

sentences.en: with Roman history, Roman precedents and so on.
sentences.zh: 罗马历史、罗马先例等等。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And essentially, by the time you get to the 9th and 10th century,
sentences.zh: 基本上，到了九、十世纪的时候，

sentences.en: what has happened is that these different stories, these different traditions, these different back projections have come to be fossilised
sentences.zh: 发生的事情是，这些不同的故事、不同的传统、不同的追溯性投射，都已经变得僵化了，

sentences.en: so that both the Welsh and the Anglo-Saxons believed that there was a kind of genuine migration.
sentences.zh: 以至于威尔士人和盎格鲁-撒克逊人都相信确实存在过某种真正的迁徙。

sentences.en: But there is, you know, in terms of the, essentially the kind of the cutting edge of academic research at the moment, there's no evidence at all for this migration.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，就目前学术界最前沿的研究而言，根本没有任何证据支持这种迁徙。

sentences.en: And so therefore, it becomes more difficult to fit Arthur into that narrative.
sentences.zh: 因此，要把亚瑟王纳入那段叙事就变得更加困难了。

sentences.en: Well, okay, let's get back stuck into Arthur.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们回到亚瑟王的话题上来。

sentences.en: The idea of there being somebody called Arthur, this incredibly romantic figure, where does that, when does that really kick in?
sentences.zh: 关于有一个叫亚瑟的人，这个极其浪漫的人物，这种想法到底是从什么时候开始真正流行的？

sentences.en: At what point are educated people swapping the story of Arthur and embellishing it?
sentences.zh: 受过教育的人是在什么时候开始交流亚瑟的故事并对其进行润色的？

sentences.en: So is this pre-Norman conquest, this becomes widespread, or is it after that?
sentences.zh: 那么，这种说法是在诺曼征服之前就广为流传，还是在那之后？

sentences.en: Well, you're getting it with Nennius, whoever Nennius was,
sentences.zh: 嗯，你在内尼厄斯（Nennius）的作品里就能看到，不管内尼厄斯是谁，

sentences.en: so you're getting it in,
sentences.zh: 所以你会在其中看到，

sentences.en: as the Anglo-Saxons are starting to kind of solidify the kingdom of England, so you are getting Arthur enshrined as a kind of folk hero for the Welsh.
sentences.zh: 随着盎格鲁-撒克逊人开始巩固英格兰王国，亚瑟作为威尔士人的某种民间英雄被供奉起来。

sentences.en: But not the Saxons, right?
sentences.zh: 但撒克逊人并不这么认为，对吧？

sentences.en: No, absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 不，绝对不是。

sentences.en: No, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不。

sentences.en: And so for...
sentences.zh: 所以对于……

sentences.en: Alfred doesn't, I mean, he either doesn't know about Arthur or he thinks Arthur is a bad guy.
sentences.zh: 阿尔弗雷德大帝并不，我是说，他要么不知道亚瑟，要么认为亚瑟是个坏人。

sentences.en: Am I right?
sentences.zh: 我说得对吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So Arthur is not mentioned by Bede, who essentially provides the only narrative that we have for what we could call the Dark Ages, and gets picked up by Alfred,
sentences.zh: 所以比德（Bede）没有提到亚瑟，他基本上提供了我们所知的“黑暗时代”唯一的叙事，而亚瑟的故事后来被阿尔弗雷德大帝所采纳，

sentences.en: who is sponsoring the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle.
sentences.zh: 他资助了《盎格鲁-撒克逊编年史》。

sentences.en: The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle doesn't mention Arthur either.
sentences.zh: 《盎格鲁-撒克逊编年史》也没有提到亚瑟。

sentences.en: So essentially,
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，

sentences.en: Arthur becomes a folk hero for the Welsh, a reminder of victories won over the Saxons, as they're called, and there's a kind of implicit sense of prophecy.
sentences.zh: 亚瑟成为了威尔士人的民间英雄，提醒着他们对所谓的撒克逊人取得的胜利，其中隐含着一种预言的意味。

sentences.en: So you also get in Nenius, I think, the first mention of Merlin.
sentences.zh: 我想，你在内尼厄斯的作品中也看到了对梅林（Merlin）的首次提及。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And with Merlin's prophecies, he is saying that the time will come where the Britons will essentially get back the lowlands,
sentences.zh: 随着梅林的预言，他说终有一天不列颠人会收复低地，

sentences.en: Loughra, they will get back England.
sentences.zh: 洛格里斯（Loughra），他们会收复英格兰。

sentences.en: And so it's this idea that Arthur will come again, that the Welsh will reverse the humiliation of their defeat.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种亚瑟会归来的想法，威尔士人会扭转他们战败的耻辱。

sentences.en: That's essentially what's powering it.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是推动这一切的动力。

sentences.en: That's all a fantasy because it never happened.
sentences.zh: 那全是幻想，因为这从未发生过。

sentences.en: Is that what you're saying?
sentences.zh: 你是这个意思吗？

sentences.en: That he's basically inventing this humiliation that never actually took place?
sentences.zh: 你是说他基本上是在编造这种从未发生过的耻辱？

sentences.en: The Anglo-Saxons, obviously they end up, you know, they identify with the more Germanic traditions to the degree that they end up speaking a Germanic language,
sentences.zh: 盎格鲁-撒克逊人显然最终认同了更多的日耳曼传统，以至于他们最终说起了日耳曼语，

sentences.en: that they take on Germanic names, that they trace their origins back to Germanic gods.
sentences.zh: 他们采用了日耳曼名字，并将自己的起源追溯到日耳曼神祇。

sentences.en: And so culturally, this then becomes dominant over the lowlands and the Romanized Christian Welsh are pushed into, as they see it, into the mountain fastnesses.
sentences.zh: 因此，在文化上，这随后在低地占据了主导地位，而罗马化的基督教威尔士人则被推向了他们眼中的山地堡垒。

sentences.en: And that's the great cultural divide.
sentences.zh: 这就是巨大的文化鸿沟。

sentences.en: And it's one of, obviously that survives the Norman conqueSt.
sentences.zh: 显然，这种鸿沟在诺曼征服后依然存在。

sentences.en: And that then muddies the waters further because essentially Arthur is an inspiration to the Welsh.
sentences.zh: 这进一步搅浑了水，因为亚瑟本质上是威尔士人的灵感来源。

sentences.en: And then also he becomes quite a potent figure for the Norman conquerors and their heirs, because again, it's kind of putting the English down.
sentences.zh: 然后，他也成为了诺曼征服者及其继承人眼中一个相当有影响力的人物，因为这同样是一种打压英格兰人的手段。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And really the guy who popularizes Arthur as a historical figure is writing in the early 12th century and that's Geoffrey of Monmouth.
sentences.zh: 真正将亚瑟作为历史人物普及开来的人，是写于12世纪初的蒙茅斯的杰弗里（Geoffrey of Monmouth）。

sentences.en: So this is Laura Lawson's question.
sentences.zh: 所以这是劳拉·劳森（Laura Lawson）的问题。

sentences.en: Laura Lawson, we should get into some questions now, I reckon.
sentences.zh: 劳拉·劳森，我想我们现在应该进入提问环节了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Because you and I can talk about King Arthur for,
sentences.zh: 因为你和我可以谈论亚瑟王……

sentences.en: I mean, maybe people were happy to hear that, but we could probably talk a witter on for days between ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我是说，也许人们很高兴听到这些，但我们俩大概能没完没了地聊上好几天。

sentences.en: But Laura Lawson says, basically, how is it, how much is it Geoffrey of Monmouth's creation?
sentences.zh: 但劳拉·劳森基本上问的是，亚瑟王的故事在多大程度上是蒙茅斯的杰弗里的创作？

sentences.en: And you think it is, right?
sentences.zh: 你认为是的，对吧？

sentences.en: I think it's,
sentences.zh: 我认为是，

sentences.en: Geoffrey of Monmouth is absolutely,
sentences.zh: 蒙茅斯的杰弗里绝对是，

sentences.en: hugely influential.
sentences.zh: 影响巨大。

sentences.en: He is constructing, he's writing a history of the kings of Britain and it's Geoffrey of Monmouth who gives the kind of the entire narrative from Brutus, the Trojan,
sentences.zh: 他正在构建，他正在撰写一部《不列颠诸王史》，正是蒙茅斯的杰弗里提供了从特洛伊的布鲁图斯（Brutus）开始的整个叙事，

sentences.en: escaping the sack of Troy, coming to Britain, killing all the giants, establishing his kingdom.
sentences.zh: 逃离特洛伊的陷落，来到不列颠，杀光所有的巨人，建立他的王国。

sentences.en: And that gives you a sense of the kind of the quality.
sentences.zh: 这让你对那种质量有了一个概念。

sentences.en: The accuracy of.
sentences.zh: 准确性的概念。

sentences.en: The accuracy.
sentences.zh: 准确性。

sentences.en: And it has to be, and he gives us a lot of the familiar story that we now know.
sentences.zh: 而且必须是，他给了我们很多现在所熟知的故事。

sentences.en: So he is the guy who weaves in the story of Arthur with Vortigern, with the arrival of Hengist and Horsa, with Merlin,
sentences.zh: 所以他就是那个将亚瑟的故事与沃蒂根（Vortigern）、亨吉斯特（Hengist）和霍萨（Horsa）的到来、梅林交织在一起的人，

sentences.en: with this idea of a golden age where Arthur becomes the king of the whole of Britain.
sentences.zh: 还有那个亚瑟成为整个不列颠之王的黄金时代的概念。

sentences.en: He invades Roman Gaul, he becomes the kind of emperor on the continent as well.
sentences.zh: 他入侵了罗马高卢，也成为了欧洲大陆上的某种皇帝。

sentences.en: So he's an all-conquering kind of superhero.
sentences.zh: 所以他是一个无往不胜的超级英雄。

sentences.en: And then there is the war between Mordred and Arthur that ends with Arthur's death, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 然后是莫德雷德（Mordred）和亚瑟之间的战争，也许以亚瑟的死告终。

sentences.en: And that then,
sentences.zh: 然后，

sentences.en: after Arthur's death, then the Britons, everything goes wrong for them.
sentences.zh: 在亚瑟死后，不列颠人的一切都变得糟糕了。

sentences.en: But I think that what is interesting, why is Geoffrey of Monmouth, what's he doing with this?
sentences.zh: 但我认为有趣的是，为什么蒙茅斯的杰弗里要这么做？他在搞什么？

sentences.en: Okay, so the last sentence of his history,
sentences.zh: 好吧，他历史书的最后一句，

sentences.en: he ends it with the reign of Athelstan.
sentences.zh: 他以埃塞尔斯坦（Athelstan）的统治结束了全书。

sentences.en: And Athelstan is the Anglo-Saxon king who joins all the various Anglo-Saxon kingdoms together to forge the kingdom of England.
sentences.zh: 埃塞尔斯坦是那位将各个盎格鲁-撒克逊王国联合起来，锻造出英格兰王国的盎格鲁-撒克逊国王。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But he also claims the supremacy over the whole of Britain.
sentences.zh: 但他同时也声称对整个不列颠拥有至高无上的权力。

sentences.en: He says he's the king of all of Britain, including the Welsh princes, including all the various kings of what will become Scotland.
sentences.zh: 他说他是整个不列颠的国王，包括威尔士诸侯，包括未来苏格兰的所有国王。

sentences.en: And Athelstan is a king who is appropriating the Roman traditions as well.
sentences.zh: 而且埃塞尔斯坦也是一位挪用罗马传统的国王。

sentences.en: So he holds kind of great derbars in Roman cities and he summons kings from across Britain.
sentences.zh: 所以他在罗马城市举行盛大的朝会，并召集来自不列颠各地的国王。

sentences.en: Does he use the word emperor, Tom?
sentences.zh: 他用了“皇帝”这个词吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: Yes, he does.
sentences.zh: 是的，他用了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So he's an imperator.
sentences.zh: 所以他是一位“统帅”（imperator）。

sentences.en: He's a rex.
sentences.zh: 他是一位“国王”（rex）。

sentences.en: He's all these kind of qualities.
sentences.zh: 他具备所有这些特质。

sentences.en: And I think it's telling that Geoffrey Monmouth finishes with Athelstan because in a sense, what he's doing is back projecting
sentences.zh: 我认为蒙茅斯的杰弗里以埃塞尔斯坦作为结尾很有深意，因为在某种意义上，他所做的是将

sentences.en: Athelstan's achievements onto the figure of Arthur.
sentences.zh: 埃塞尔斯坦的成就投射到了亚瑟身上。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So I think that Arthur is a kind of a Britannised Athelstan, if you like.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为亚瑟是一个“不列颠化”的埃塞尔斯坦，如果你愿意这么说的话。

sentences.en: He's an emperor who rules over the whole of Britain, who is the heir to Roman traditions, who achieves great things and defeats his enemies.
sentences.zh: 他是一位统治整个不列颠的皇帝，是罗马传统的继承者，成就了伟大的事业并击败了他的敌人。

sentences.en: And I think essentially that that's what's going on.
sentences.zh: 我认为本质上这就是正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: And I think as well, it's telling that there are Welsh writers who are aware that this is absolute nonsense.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为同样说明问题的是，有一些威尔士作家意识到这完全是胡说八道。

sentences.en: There's Gerald of Wales.
sentences.zh: 比如威尔士的杰拉尔德（Gerald of Wales）。

sentences.en: He's splendidly named Gerald of Wales.
sentences.zh: 他有一个响亮的名字叫威尔士的杰拉尔德。

sentences.en: Gerald of Wales.
sentences.zh: 威尔士的杰拉尔德。

sentences.en: Who describes a man who's possessed by devils.
sentences.zh: 他描述了一个被恶魔附身的人。

sentences.en: And he says that when the Gospels are placed on the chest of this possessed man, the devils flee away.
sentences.zh: 他说当福音书放在这个被附身的人胸口时，恶魔就会逃走。

sentences.en: But if you put a copy of Geoffrey of Monmouth's history on his chest, all the devils come flocking back.
sentences.zh: 但如果你把一本蒙茅斯的杰弗里的历史书放在他胸口，所有的恶魔都会蜂拥而回。

sentences.en: That's historians.
sentences.zh: 这就是历史学家。

sentences.en: That's just historians being bitchy about each other, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这只是历史学家之间互相刻薄，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there's a kind of kickback against the fact that Geoffrey is writing history.
sentences.zh: 所以对于杰弗里在写历史这件事，有一种反弹。

sentences.en: But obviously, you know, people have a stake.
sentences.zh: 但显然，你知道，人们都有利害关系。

sentences.en: The Welsh have a stake in it.
sentences.zh: 威尔士人对此有利害关系。

sentences.en: So they're generally quite keen on it.
sentences.zh: 所以他们通常对此很热衷。

sentences.en: And of course, the kings of England have a stake in it.
sentences.zh: 当然，英格兰的国王们对此也有利害关系。

sentences.en: Because if Arthur was the king of the whole of Britain, then obviously that's quite useful.
sentences.zh: 因为如果亚瑟是整个不列颠的国王，那显然非常有用。

sentences.en: If you're a Norman king wanting to conquer the Welsh, wanting to conquer the Scots.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一位想要征服威尔士人、想要征服苏格兰人的诺曼国王的话。

sentences.en: And because Arthur had invaded and conquered much of the Roman Empire, according to Geoffrey of Monmouth, it's also quite useful if you want to launch a continental invasion.
sentences.zh: 而且根据蒙茅斯的杰弗里的说法，因为亚瑟曾经入侵并征服了大部分罗马帝国，如果你想发动一场大陆入侵，这也很有用。

sentences.en: So that's essentially the kind of the context for Arthur that we get by the Middle Ages.
sentences.zh: 所以这基本上就是我们在中世纪所得到的关于亚瑟的背景。

sentences.en: He's of use to the kings of England.
sentences.zh: 他对英格兰国王们很有用。

sentences.en: And so that's the point at which I guess he gets picked up by the Corkley kind of tradition, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 所以我想这就是他被克雷蒂安（Chrétien）那种传统所采纳的时刻，不是吗？

sentences.en: Chrétien de Troyes and then Mallory and all the rest of it.
sentences.zh: 克雷蒂安·德·特鲁瓦（Chrétien de Troyes），然后是马洛里（Mallory）等等。

sentences.en: But you did.
sentences.zh: 但是你确实……

sentences.en: There's one thing we haven't gone into.
sentences.zh: 有一件事我们还没深入探讨。

sentences.en: So this has started to come up a lot in recent years.
sentences.zh: 近年来，这个问题开始频繁出现。

sentences.en: We have a question from Killing Me Softly.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个来自“Killing Me Softly”的问题。

sentences.en: I know who he is.
sentences.zh: 我知道他是谁。

sentences.en: He's a TV producer called Mick McAvoy.
sentences.zh: 他是一位名叫米克·麦卡沃伊（Mick McAvoy）的电视制片人。

sentences.en: And he says, there's a lot of evidence.
sentences.zh: 他说，有很多证据。

sentences.en: He says that King Arthur was from Scotland.
sentences.zh: 他说亚瑟王来自苏格兰。

sentences.en: We have a Ben Arthur and Arthur's seat.
sentences.zh: 我们有本亚瑟山（Ben Arthur）和亚瑟王座（Arthur's Seat）。

sentences.en: Merlin has been linked to the ancient royal family based at Dumbarton Rock.
sentences.zh: 梅林与以邓巴顿岩（Dumbarton Rock）为基地的古代皇室有关联。

sentences.en: So was King Arthur Scottish?
sentences.zh: 所以亚瑟王是苏格兰人吗？

sentences.en: How unlike a Scottish listener to write something that something is Scottish and that the English have stolen it.
sentences.zh: 苏格兰听众写信说某样东西是苏格兰的，而且被英格兰人偷走了，这太像苏格兰人的风格了。

sentences.en: Oh, indeed, the Welsh have stolen it.
sentences.zh: 哦，确实，威尔士人也偷走了它。

sentences.en: So do you think, or is that, well, one answer might be that Scottish and Welsh are kind of the same in this period, that there's no clear distinction between the two.
sentences.zh: 所以你认为，或者说，一个答案可能是苏格兰人和威尔士人在那个时期差不多是一样的，两者之间没有明确的区别。

sentences.en: Would that be completely untoward, Tom?
sentences.zh: 这会完全不妥吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: Well, the Welsh speakers who give us this early romance where, this epic where you get he was no Arthur.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那些给我们带来早期浪漫史的威尔士语使用者，那部史诗里提到他不是亚瑟。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, they're Welsh speakers.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们是威尔士语使用者。

sentences.en: So those traditions, the traditions of Arthur, the traditions of a great warlord who fought
sentences.zh: 所以那些传统，亚瑟的传统，一位伟大的军阀与

sentences.en: the Angles and the Saxons, that's as true if you're a Welsh speaker in, you know, Dumbarton, one of the great rock of Dumbarton, as it is if you're in what we'd now call Wales.
sentences.zh: 盎格鲁人和撒克逊人作战的传统，如果你是一位在邓巴顿——邓巴顿那块伟大的岩石——的威尔士语使用者，这同样适用，就像你在我们现在所说的威尔士一样。

sentences.en: So in that sense, I think, yes, Arthur is a kind of mythic figure for all those who are speaking kind of variants of Welsh.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个意义上说，我认为，是的，亚瑟对于所有说威尔士语变体的人来说，都是一个神话人物。
